title: Screens and help articles (inventory.json)
description: The input of tour-inventory and help-refs (standard/help-system.md, "The tour manifest"): every screen by its key, whether the menu reaches it, and its help article's numbered tasks in order, each naming the tour that shows it and the anchor ids of the controls it mentions. A project writes it, or generates it from its help content folder and its menu.

anchorWindows.description: For every control that recordAnchors lists, on any screen, the window it sits in: the id of the window a need reopens to reach it (appt.drawer, pay.sheet, appt.create), or "screen" for a resolver's own control on the screen itself, the one a step opens her record through (cal.ended-appointment). Anchor ids are global, so the map is one, at the root. An id that sits in two windows (the same control in her drawer and in a sheet) gets its own id in each. With --inventory the checker requires an entry for every listed id and none for an id no recordAnchors lists (window-missing, window-extra); a do step at on: sample on a listed control in a window, the step that opens her record through it included, names a need whose last reopen is the window this map gives for its control (need-window, and sample-no-need when it names none); "screen" serves only the step that opens her record through a recordOpen result naming that control (screen-anchor); and the step at on: none before the picker opened the window this map gives for the picker's control, and every later do step's control sits in that window until a step that opens her record (picker-window). The checker trusts the map: the inventory's reviewer opens each listed control in the running app and confirms the window it sits in, or that it sits on the screen itself; that the bindings can reopen each window named here is the bindings' (the suite checks the example's).

recordAnchors.description: The anchors of this screen that resolve to the sample's own record, and only those: a resolver's own id that picks the sample's row (cal.ended-appointment), and every control inside a window, card or sheet opened on her (her appointment, payment, chat, document). An id that every person's row in a list carries, the row's plain id (cal.appointment, patients.row) or a control on each row (patients.charge), binds the first visible row, a real person's whenever the sample is not first: it is a container and goes in containerAnchors, never here. A control that acts on many people's records at once goes in bulkAnchors, never here. Anchor ids are global: an id listed on one screen counts on every screen. Each listed id names the window its control sits in, in anchorWindows at the inventory's root. A do step at on: none on one of them, or whose result names one, is a finding; a do step at on: sample on one of them comes after an earlier do step at on: sample in the same tour, on the same device, that opened her record (a recordOpen result that names the step's own control, a resolver's own id) or picked her (the picker exception: an unclassed pick step with a custom result, after the do step at on: none, on that device and under no other condition, that opened its window), unless it is that step itself, and, unless it is that step, names a need that reopens the window its control sits in, with selectSample as well where that window picks a person (the checker requires it on every step after the picker; the picker's own step names the reopen too, and so does an opener whose control anchorWindows puts in a window: only the opener on the screen itself, a control anchorWindows marks screen, names no need); the engine runs that need each time the run reaches the step: a reopen is skipped only when its window is already open on her (isOpen; a window that picks a person counts as open only while it is the tour's own and every person field it has holds only the sample, or is empty (a person field names whose record the step acts on, a patient or a client, a second one such as a family member or a referrer included, and a field that lists several people holds only the sample when she is the only one in it; a field that names staff, such as the therapist, is not one, and a binding that counts it anyway only makes the reopen run more often)), and selectSample runs after the reopen, and the need lists them in that order: every reopen closes what it replaces without saving it, through that window's own close, and where a window's own close saves, its reopen is not a need and the step only shows; a reopen of a window that picks a person closes any other window of that kind (an existing appointment's edit form included) and opens the tour's own afresh with every person field empty, so isOpen holds after it; the tour's own is the new window the tour's step opened, never an existing record's window at the same slot; the need's last reopen names the window the inventory's anchorWindows gives for the step's control; a control anchorWindows marks screen, a resolver's own control on the screen itself, is acted on only by the step that opens her record through it; a step that opens her record through a control inside a window reopens that window on her first, as every other step there does (a window opened on one person, such as a patient card, counts as open only while it shows the sample's record); the do step before the picker opened the window anchorWindows gives for the picker's control, and every later do step's control sits in that window until a step that opens her record; selectSample runs only in the tour's own window, the one the step's reopen just opened or found open on her, and only where that window picks a person: the engine passes it the id of the window the need's last reopen names, and it picks her there, asks nothing, never runs in a window that holds an existing record, and reports whether the sample is now picked in the tour's own window. The need asks one thing: before a reopen closes a form that holds her input, it asks, saying her changes there will be lost; when she declines, nothing is closed and selectSample does not run; when she declines, or selectSample does not report the sample picked, the step only shows, and every later do step of the tour only shows too, never pressing, across a resume and on another device, until a later reopen she accepts opens the tour's own afresh (and, where the need names selectSample, it reports her picked). A do step at on: sample on a control no recordAnchors lists is a finding: when the control sits in a window opened on her (a step before it in the tour opened it on her), the fix is in the inventory (list it here and keep on: sample); when it sits on her row in a list, light it through a resolver's own id that picks her row and list that id; only a control that is nobody's record changes the step, a save there is a stop step, and this finding is never answered by setting on: none. The one exception: a control that picks a person in a window opened on nobody (a patient picker), where picking saves and sends nothing by itself, is listed here; its do step carries no class, and its result checks that the sample was picked (a custom result, as appt.sample-picked). That window's other controls (appt.service, appt.save) are listed with it, and a do step on one of them comes only after the picker's step. A picker that saves or sends as it picks (it adds the person to a list, assigns or invites her) is a stop step, never a do step, and the rows of a picker's list are containers. A listed id covers every arg of its family, so a control that exports, prints or acts on many people, or that sits on a person's record, gets its own id and is never one arg of a family whose other members differ. A filter, a sort or a search acts on no record and is in none of the three lists. The project declares them; that the list is complete is judged in the running app.

bulkAnchors.description: The anchors of this screen that export, print, download, share, import or otherwise act on many people's records at once (select all, a bulk send, a bulk delete, an import, cal.print). A tour never does one: a do step on one of them, or whose result names one, is a finding at any on and any class; a showing or a stop step on it is fine, and a stop step on an export or a print is classed T, since data leaves. A listed id covers every arg of its family, so a control that exports, prints or acts on many people, or that sits on a person's record, gets its own id and is never one arg of a family whose other members differ. A filter, a sort or a search acts on no record and is in none of the three lists. An id is in at most one of recordAnchors, bulkAnchors and containerAnchors. The project declares them; that the list is complete is judged in the running app.

containerAnchors.description: The anchors of this screen whose element holds people's rows or records (a list, a column, the calendar grid), and every id that each row of such a list carries (the row's plain id, as cal.appointment or patients.row, or a control on each row, as patients.charge), which binds the first visible row. On a do step the lit target is live, so a do step lit on a container lets her press any person's row inside it, or the first visible row: that is a finding at any on and any class, and a tour lights the sample's own row or control at on: sample, through a resolver's own id that picks it and is listed in recordAnchors (as cal.ended-appointment, never the plain id every row carries), or, for an empty slot, the slot through a resolver (cal.free-slot) at on: none. A person picker in a window opened on nobody, where picking saves and sends nothing, is in recordAnchors instead; the rows of its list are containers. A result that names a container, on a step at on: none, is a finding too. An id is in at most one of the three lists. The project declares them; that the list is complete is judged in the running app.

viewOf.description: This key is a view of that screen (the calendar's day view of its week): a core entry may group a screen's views, and they count as one core screen.

menu.description: The screen is reachable from the menu.

tasks.description: The article's numbered tasks, in their order.

text.description: The task's name, as the tours list it in tasks.

tour.description: The tour that shows this task (its first chapter for a job).

anchors.description: The anchor ids of the controls the task's text mentions.
